results.summary:
The dispatcher now names the session behind a background attempt one tick after its launch, so the attempts that never file a terminal verb — crashed, timed_out, protocol_violation — still carry session_id and transcript_path when they are written off. Draft PR #137.

New `jobSessionUpdate(attempt, job, root = jobsDir())` in src/jobs.js: reads the job record via the same `currentSession` #135 uses (handed a synthesized CLAUDE_JOB_DIR, which is the only way to read a job this process is not inside), falls back to the listing's own `sessionId` while the record says nothing, and goes through the same `sessionUpdate` from src/model.js. Fills blanks only — a row a verb has stamped is byte-identical afterwards — and refuses to write at all when the record names a session the row does not (a resumed job is one record over two sessions, so pairing the verb's id with the record's transcript would describe two).

src/dispatch.js calls it once, inside the reclaim branch that had already resolved the job for the liveness check: no new subprocess, no per-attempt API call. The branch's writes are now batched behind one `dirty` flag saved after the outcome is known, so an attempt written off in the same tick that named its session costs one PATCH instead of two (failAttempt saves the same record).

Nothing in #135 was rebuilt or duplicated: no second field set, no second marker, no hook. The Stop hook and the terminal verb still win on any row they reach first, and can still add the cost fields the job record does not carry.

Scope note for the reviewer: the card said to touch only src/dispatch.js, src/jobs.js and test/jobs.test.js, but two wiki lines described the terminal verb as the only path to a recorded session and AGENTS.md asks for the covering page to be updated in the same change. docs/wiki/architecture/overview.md and docs/wiki/GLOSSARY.md carry a targeted correction; the page is deliberately NOT re-stamped, since it was already stale from earlier commits I did not re-verify.
